traces.description: the same four bars, over and over, and then nothing
the child never did get the passage right

anchors.timing: while the lesson was still going on overhead

anchors.name: the fuse going in the building

traces.description: a crack in the cellar and every light on the riser out at once
candle smoke on the ceilings of everyone who sat it out

anchors.sceneTiming: the lights on that riser were dead from then until the morning

candidates.text: Patrick Brennan claims to have been at the Arcadia dance hall at 10:30 PM but cannot say that the challenger went down in the fourth and the crowd booed it, which everybody there can.

Rufus Tillman carries the mark of it: candle smoke on the ceilings of everyone who sat it out. That fixes Rufus Tillman at the vestibule of the Hallam apartments at 9:00 PM, when the fuse going in the building happened.
Found at the victim’s house on the back lot: A promissory note for $4,000 signed by Rufus Tillman, endorsed to Nora Mulcahy, three months past due.
Verity Coffin says Nora Mulcahy told Rufus Tillman that Friday was the end of it, one way or the other.
Found at the Arcadia dance hall: A draft codicil in Nora Mulcahy’s hand striking Nunzio Moretti out of the will, dated last Tuesday and unsigned.
Agnes Callahan says Nora Mulcahy told Nunzio Moretti the lawyer was coming Thursday and that the arrangement would be changed.
Found at the vestibule of the Hallam apartments: A typed page of dates and sums in Nora Mulcahy’s file, headed with Patrick Brennan’s name.
Althea Mosley says Nora Mulcahy told Patrick Brennan that the story would run whether Patrick Brennan liked it or not.
Found at the victim’s house on the back lot: A clipping about the failure of Althea Mosley’s business, with Nora Mulcahy’s name underlined twice in pencil.
Cornelius Hanrahan says Althea Mosley said Nora Mulcahy had taken everything and would be made to feel it.
Margarethe Hauck hired us. Margarethe Hauck wants it known that Rufus Tillman owed the victim money, and would rather we started there.
Gittel Zeldin on Rufus Tillman: Rufus Tillman’s sleeves are buttoned at the wrist in a warm room.
Hattie Whitfield on Rufus Tillman: Somebody at the chop suey place over the laundry sells what a druggist will not, and Rufus Tillman knows which door.
Nunzio Moretti on Rufus Tillman: Rufus Tillman was steady at nine and shaking at seven, and it was not nerves about the police.
A paper of powder at the chop suey place over the laundry, folded the way one particular hand folds them.
A prescription blank at the chop suey place over the laundry signed by a doctor who has been dead since the spring.
The man who sells it at the chop suey place over the laundry gives it up rather than be held: Rufus Tillman was there from 11:00 PM to 11:30 PM, and stayed until it took hold.
